master.note: Built locally, NOT by the firmware team's release toolchain. BYTE-IDENTICAL to 1.2.3 except the version byte (two bytes differ): this release changes follower-only code, and the leader is rebuilt solely to keep both roles on one version number. 1.2.5 makes that policy structural -- 1.2.3 aligned the two numbers but left two #ifdef-guarded version definitions in the source, so the drift cause survived; 1.2.5 collapses them into one, and a role can no longer be left behind. The 1.2.3 leader validation therefore still stands (TCGU01A28Z0023m / 0024m: version reports, encoder and IMU both read at 9.72 / 9.64 m/s^2 at rest, ~100 Hz data stream over 2 s, and an unassigned command code answers ProtocolError(NACK: InvalidCmd), which is what proves the V2.3 error semantics reached this role). POWER-CYCLE THE GRIPPER AFTER FLASHING.

slave.note: Built locally, NOT by the firmware team's release toolchain. Hardware-validated on TCGU01A28Z0018s. The closed zero written by auto-calibration (min_open_rad) goes to 0, so normalized 0.0 is the closed hard stop itself instead of an inset short of it: six open/close cycles land at raw -0.00049 with 0.383 mrad of spread, arrived true and HOLDING_POSITION throughout, against -0.02014 on 1.2.3 -- 19.65 mrad tighter. A five-minute continuous hold does not drift, decays 1.2% in torque and warms +1.0 C, flat within the sensor's 1 C resolution after 90 s. The two earlier insets (20 mrad, then 5 mrad) were measured against premises that no longer held; a pure feed-forward sweep (kp=kd=0) settled it -- 0.15 Nm seats the jaw at raw +0.00000 and 0.20/0.30/0.40/0.50 Nm move it no further, so raw 0 is a hard stop, no inset is needed, and more torque buys no closure. Seating is the SDK's job now (ForcePositionConfig::close_preload_nm, 0.25 Nm default). Earlier 1.2.3 follower validation still applies: auto-calibration 11 s -> 1.3 s, idle status stream stays fresh, instruction-5 fault reads keep advancing. POWER-CYCLE THE GRIPPER AFTER FLASHING (24 V, not just USB).
